extracted.intended_audience: public information officers, JIC planners, IMT members, MAC Group/agency administrators involved in incident communications
extracted.subtask_description: An operating guide for establishing, staffing, activating, and running a Joint Information Center (JIC) to coordinate public, media, and political communications during a major incident (wildfire and other disasters). Covers roles, responsibilities, activation/transition, section-level duties, staffing, facilities, and release protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC is the single point of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: A Joint Information Center (JIC) is an information facility that is the single point of contact during an ongoing major incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary customers include directly affected public, general public, all agencies/organizations involved or affected, elected/appointed officials at every level, and all media (local, regional, national/international). The purpose is to ensure emergency information is "spoken with one clear voice" and has been coordinated and approved through the appropriate chain of command. FEMA involvement may change chain-of-command relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accurate and timely coordinated information
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIC will be the focal point for providing accurate and timely coordinated information concerning the incident; its goal is a single point where public and media can receive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information should aim to reduce/eliminate loss of life or injury, minimize human suffering, and support the length of the catastrophe response. All releases should be coordinated with IMT as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC reports to and takes direction from the MAC Group
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Information Center will report directly to the Multiagency Coordination Group (MAC Group) and the JIC Center Manager will receive general direction from the MAC Group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MAC Group direction is usually limited to non-operational matters and broad overview; matters affecting all agencies or emerging issues should be referred to MAC Group for guidance/resolution. JIC will operate under MAC Group oversight to ensure smooth information flow and issue resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize JIC into six service areas with section leads
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIC will contain six service areas: 1) Community Information, 2) Media Relations, 3) Political/Elected Officials, 4) Disaster Services & Law Enforcement, 5) Internal Communications, and 6) Web Management. Each section will have a Section Manager or Lead Information Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section has specific responsibilities both as JIC duties and for the entities they represent; section leads coordinate "up and down" their service area and should document roles, responsibilities, and coordination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section leaders must develop protocols and document coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Section Leader will develop protocols and document the daily coordination activities within his/her agency/organization/volunteer group outlining all key contacts at all levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first contact should establish whether subsequent contact frequency is hourly, daily, every other day, or incident-activity dependent. Protocols should include political contacts and internal JIC coordination; MAC Group and MAST PR Team should select section leaders early so staffing and protocols can be prepared before activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint an interim JIC Center Manager available 24/7
rubrics_metrics.description: An interim JIC Center Manager should be identified before activation, available 24 hours a day, seven days a week at a moment's notice. This interim lead could become the permanent lead if directed by the MAC Group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon IMT arrival the IC, Team IIO, MAST PR representatives, interim JIC Manager, and MAC Group representatives will evaluate the JIC manager position and decide on permanent leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activate JIC immediately when IMT is ordered; target 6-hour readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIC will be activated at the same time any Incident Management Team (IMT) is ordered by Agency Administrators. One primary goal is to have the JIC activated and operating within 6 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interim manager and section leads are pre-identified, they will be ordered at the same time. Timing should err on the side of immediacy; rolling initial attack resources into the JIC upon activation is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify initial-attack Lead IIO and transition process
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which agency Information Officer has the initial attack lead in advance so they know where to respond in the field or whether multiple should respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve immediately who should be the lead during initial attack (jurisdiction-based decision). As fire goes beyond initial attack, agencies activate information centers; these should not try to replicate JIC scale—local resources handle initial onslaught until JIC activation and roll-over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Authority must outline information entity authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Delegation of Authority (FSM 5132.03) should outline the authorities of all incident information entities including the role of the JIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Unified Command exists, operational procedures to meet each agency's needs should be discussed and documented in the Delegation of Authority. MAC Group members may express concerns or requirements at IMT briefings.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMT Team briefing must cover JIC roles and information-release authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately following the transition meeting, the IMT, Forest PAO, MAST PR Team, and JIC Lead will meet to discuss JIC roles/responsibilities, Unified Command and MAC Group roles, staffing, and designation of JIC Center Manager or IIO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss releases concerning evacuations, injuries, fatalities, press conferences, media management, and approving authorities to reach a common understanding about information release and approving processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC Center Manager responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIC Center Manager is the overall Lead Information Officer responsible for coordination and management of the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include ensuring adequate staffing levels, meeting equipment needs, resolving health and safety issues, ensuring IMT needs are met, identifying number of co-leads needed for 24-hour operations, and taking broad direction from the MAC Group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Information section primary responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Information will share and disseminate information of interest to local and regional communities and has six primary responsibilities: respond to citizen inquiries; coordinate with IMT's; web-based information coordination; use Fire Safe Councils; coordinate volunteers; distribute information internally to other JIC sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing upon activation: preliminary 10, full 15; minimum staff should include federal (USFS), state (CDF), county fire, sheriff, and Fire Safe Council representative; consider adding social science specialist. Community Lead should be a qualified PIO with extensive wildland fire community experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Information operational guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Community section must ensure accurate and approved information is coordinated with the IMT prior to public dissemination and has delegated authority to interact with community contacts according to agreed system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use approved IMT/statutory agency information, refer callers to IMT or other authorities as appropriate, provide logistical support for community meetings, use fax/e-mail lists or phone trees for direct feeds, establish mental health disaster advisor connections, develop Critical Incident Stress Team protocol, and create volunteer directories. Close coordination with IMT, Disaster Assessment Team, evacuation centers, and State/County OES is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: All reports and fact sheets concise and JIC-manager approved
rubrics_metrics.description: All reports, fact sheets or other information should be concise and approved by the JIC manager prior to public release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies across sections; the JIC manager should review content for conciseness and approval. Time-critical releases may follow specified expedited procedures elsewhere (e.g., news release process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Relations section primary responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Relations serves as a primary media contact with five primary responsibilities: coordinate with IMT Incident Information Officer; coordinate with emergency service sections; respond to media inquiries; coordinate/supervise video contractor; prepare and disseminate daily summarized update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JIC serves as support for IMT IIO but has delegated authority to issue news releases independent of IMT. Coordination with emergency services ensures information is gathered from statutory units based on their approval of releasable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: News release authority, content sourcing and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: JIC has delegated authority to develop regularly scheduled and timely news releases; releases are developed based upon approved statutory agency guidelines and should have IMT IIO, MAC Group, or on-site JIC interagency representatives review drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A release may be transmitted without such a review if time constraints warrant. News releases should be provided to all JIC section leaders. For USFS, WO Media Desk approval is not needed for national media interviews during fire emergencies, but talking points should be coordinated through IMT and MAC Group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media staff authority and coordination expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: JIC media staffers have delegated authority to respond independently to media reporters via telephone, TV interviews, or e-mail requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While staffers may respond independently, talking points and significant messaging should be coordinated through the IMT and MAC Group. Establish 'roll-over' procedures for transferring media callers from partner facilities to JIC and ensure partners receive timely news releases/fact sheets to maintain consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fatality event communications protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: For fatality events, consult Agency Administrators Guide to Critical Incident Management (PMS 926/NFES 1356) and coordinate communications with the JIC manager, IMT and MAC Group for specific procedures and assignment of roles/responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced NWCG guidance and ensure interagency coordination for sensitive communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure loss information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Damage Assessment Team, IMT or MAC Group will provide the JIC manager information about extent of structure loss; if information is not immediately available, JIC manager will provide name/contact for media inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMT and JIC must work closely when planning release of information about structures; ensure accuracy and timely coordination before public dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evacuations and road closures led by statutory agency
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory agency will take the lead through its JIC involvement for coordinating release of current information on evacuations and road closures; the lead statutory office must confirm information prior to public release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate releases with the statutory lead to avoid conflicting or premature information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media/technical facilities and supplies minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to develop JIC workstations for specified minimum staffing and provide communications/equipment capabilities: phones, unpublished lines, rollover/rolling ring systems, fax machines, televisions, recorders, cable service, radio scanners, computers/printers, maps, and office supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community section: workstations for minimum 11 with expansion to 15; Media section: minimum 10 workstations and programmable fax; Political section: minimum 3 workstations. Publicize JIC telephone number and likely staffing schedule. Prepare desk guides and media contact lists immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing minimums and qualification expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section specifies minimum staffing levels and recommends qualified leads (e.g., Information Officer, Type 1 qualification for Media/Disaster Services leads, PIOs with wildland fire experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Community section initial 10/adaptable to 15; Media Relations full minimum 6 information officers per 24-hour shift; Disaster Services minimum staff 10 per 24-hour shift. Section leads should be experienced incident information officers, with suggested candidate names provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political/Elected Officials section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: This section provides information to elected officials and agency leaders; primary responsibilities: clearinghouse for timely information, develop approved briefing reports, coordinate VIP tours, and lead national/state briefings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing minimums include federal (USFS), state (CDF), county fire (OES) PIOs; leaders should understand wildland fire and be able to communicate politically sensitive issues. Prepare briefing papers and responsive letters, coordinate IMT support for VIP visits, and maintain protocols for political contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster Services & Law Enforcement section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports IMTs and statutory evacuation/road management agencies by serving as a clearinghouse for information flows and providing cleared/approved information for JIC web posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum staffing includes USFS, CDF, county fire, county sheriff, CalTrans, CHP, County OES, Southern California Edison, Red Cross; lead should be Type 1 qualified with evacuation/structure-loss experience. Assign an information officer to the Damage Assessment Team; prepare fact sheets and coordinate evacuation/road status information for all sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish pre-incident desk guides and contact lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations to establish ASAP phone tree contact lists, desk guides on community key contacts, and JIC workstations/equipment before incident onset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop desk guide on community key contacts, JIC media contact desk guides, and a key contact list of elected officials and agency headquarters. These should be available in the JIC library for rapid use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate closely with IMT, South Ops, and partner agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Close coordination with IMT, MAC Group, Disaster Assessment Team, Evacuation Centers/Shelters, State/County OES, South Ops and statutory agencies is essential for consistent and accurate information flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish liaison at JIC to work with South Ops and place an information person with the IMT to convey incident information to JIC. Use established channels to ensure cross-section information sharing and avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC support role for Disaster Recovery Center when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: On rare occasions, such as when requested by FEMA, the JIC could take on a role within the Disaster Recovery Center (DRC), providing information support to disaster relief agencies, organizations, and volunteer groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to adapt JIC functions to support DRC operations and coordinate with disaster relief agencies and volunteer groups dealing with victims and survivors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop response plans for mass trauma and special topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a response plan for mass trauma (fatalities, structure loss) in conjunction with MAC Group, IMTs and other JIC sections and obtain subject-matter experts (e.g., animal damage/lost pet consultants, mental health advisors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate across sections, prepare fact sheets, and assign appropriate information officers to specialized teams (Damage Assessment, casualty teams). Ensure mental health and Critical Incident Stress Team protocols are in place for JIC personnel and public outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily task lists and coordination for community events
rubrics_metrics.description: The Community Section should develop a task list for each day's planned community events and ensure information transmission between IMT and the community section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any questions about community events or situations should be facilitated through the IMT Information Officer to avoid duplication and ensure accuracy.
